record_type_quote:
In the ninth installment of
Data Replicada
, we report our attempt to replicate a recently published
Journal of Marketing Research
(JMR) article entitled, “Advertising a Desired Change: When Process Simulation Fosters (vs. Hinders) Credibility and Persuasion” (
.htm
).

targets.title: Advertising a Desired Change: When Process Simulation Fosters (vs. Hinders) Credibility and Persuasion
targets.evidence_quote: We chose to replicate Study 2 (N = 213) because (1) it, along with Study 3, represented the simplest test of the authors’ hypothesis, and (2) it contained stronger statistical evidence (ps  < .01) than Study 3 (p = .02).
targets.outcome_quote: In sum, this was an unambiguous success. We of course can’t speak to all of the studies in this paper, but we can confidently conclude that people judge this progression weight loss ad to be more credible than these Before/After ads.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall verdict covers both new-sample replications of Study 2.

reasoning: Full blog article by Joe and Leif matches assigned title and byline. It reports two preregistered new-sample replications. The target title is explicitly given and linked, but the article supplies no reference-list authors or year and no printed DOI, so these remain empty.
